answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a stake that only unlocks after verified work: a newcomer starts at its nadir, with zero reputation and throttled access, and climbs only by completing attested jobs. Reputation then grows like a trellis — each endorsement links to a real completed transaction, so a fake cluster has no genuine edges to climb on. To fake a thousand trusted agents, an attacker must fund a thousand stakes and pay for a thousand real jobs, turning cheap identity forgery into a knoll of sunk cost that dwarfs any reward from one fake vote or listing.
